extracted.intended_audience: hospitals, health system administrators, episode-based payment model participants, and stakeholders submitting comments on the CJR-X proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and specification of pricing, target-price construction, risk adjustment, trend adjustment, outlier handling, and payment attribution rules for the proposed CJR-X episode-based payment model (MS-DRG/HCPCS episodes, regional benchmarks, 90-day post-discharge episodes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite quality score methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: A composite quality score that combines multiple, complementary quality measures into a single assessment of hospital performance across the episode of care, incorporating measures of patient safety, patient experience, and patient-reported outcomes (definitions and methodology at proposed §512.635(b)(1)/(2) and §512.605).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification: avoids over-reliance on any single metric, improves reliability/stability by mitigating random variation, recognizes achievement and incentivizes progress across participants, promotes equitable comparisons and predictability in reconciliation outcomes. Example arithmetic shown (e.g., 10% inpatient * 17.00 + 90% outpatient * 14.00 = 14.3). CMS seeks comment on the proposed methodology and definitions at cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3‑year baseline period and rolling/weighting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use three years of baseline episode spending, rolled forward every year, to calculate benchmark prices that are then adjusted to create preliminary target prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline years defined as the 3 fiscal years in a baseline period (example FY2024, FY2025, FY2026 for PY1). CMS proposes weighting baseline year 1 at 17%, year 2 at 33%, and year 3 at 50% (temporal weighting to emphasize more recent data). CMS provides examples for how the cadence rolls forward for PY1 and PY2 and seeks comment on these definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional target pricing (100% regional data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide target prices for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region based on 100 percent regional data, making CJR‑X an achievement-based model (participants compete against regional peers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with hospital-specific pricing: regional pricing requires achievement vs improvement, avoids having historically efficient hospitals penalized by competing with their own lower historical spending. CMS seeks comment on using regional target prices for all participants as described at §512.640(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark price calculation (MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type & region)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use average standardized spending for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type in each region (after capping high-cost outliers) as the benchmark price for that episode type/region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to cap high-cost outliers at the 99th percentile before computing benchmarks; the methodology would yield 36 MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type/region-level benchmark prices. Benchmark prices are then adjusted by prospective trend, prospective normalization, risk multipliers, and a discount factor to yield preliminary target prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary target price construction (formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary Target Price = Benchmark Price * Prospective Trend Factor * Prospective Normalization Factor * Risk Adjustment Multipliers * Discount Factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: prospective trend factor estimates expected change in spending between baseline and performance year; prospective normalization factor prevents overall inflation of target prices due to risk adjustment (subject to limited reconciliation adjustment); risk multipliers adjust for patient and facility characteristics; discount factor represents Medicare's portion of potential savings. CMS will use standardized payment data for calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment multipliers and variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk adjust episode-level target prices at reconciliation by facility bed-size and safety net status and by beneficiary-level variables: age group, HCC (Hierarchical Condition Category) count, beneficiary economic risk, prior post-acute care use, disability status as reason for initial Medicare enrollment, and recent medical history (22 separate binary indicators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk adjustment multipliers are calculated prospectively at the MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type level based on baseline data and held fixed for the performance year. Hospital-level adjusters (bed size, safety net) are included. After risk adjusting, CMS proposes to normalize to ensure the average of total risk-adjusted preliminary target prices does not exceed the average of the total non-risk-adjusted preliminary target prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective normalization factor and reconciliation cap (+/−5%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate a prospective normalization factor based on the data used to calculate risk adjustment multipliers and apply it to the benchmark price when forming preliminary target prices; allow a limited reconciliation adjustment to the normalization factor not to exceed +/−5% of the prospective normalization factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure that risk adjustment does not inflate target prices overall. The final normalization factor may be adjusted at reconciliation based on observed performance period case mix but within the +/−5% bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-cost outlier cap at 99th percentile
rubrics_metrics.description: Cap both baseline episode spending and performance-year episode spending at the 99th percentile of spending for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type, region, and baseline year (the 'high-cost outlier cap').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS moved away from a 2-standard-deviation cap to a 99th-percentile cap based on past experience. Capped spending is used when calculating benchmarks and when computing performance-year episode spending at reconciliation so participants are not held responsible for catastrophic spending. Example: if cap = $30,000 and actual spending = $45,000, spending is reduced to $30,000 for model calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective and retrospective trend-factor approach with +/-3% reconciliation cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a prospective trend factor to preliminary target prices and apply a retrospective trend-factor adjustment at reconciliation (the retrospective adjustment is capped at +/−3% of the prospective trend factor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: combine predictability (prospective target prices) with correction for realized performance-year spending patterns (retrospective adjustment). This aligns with TEAM's approach; CJR‑X will not include TEAM's two trend years in the prospective trend. CMS provides historical context (earlier models used larger caps such as +/−10% and +/−5%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration of payments for services that extend beyond the episode
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Medicare payment spans care both inside and outside the 90-day episode window, prorate the payment so only the portion attributable to care during the episode is attributed to the episode payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed proration methods: for non-IPPS inpatient and inpatient PAC services (e.g., CAH, SNF, IRF, LTCH, IPF) prorate by percentage of actual length of stay (days) falling within the episode window. For HHA services prorate based on percentage of days between first and last billable service that fall within the episode. For IPPS services, prorate the normal MS-DRG payment amount based on the geometric mean length of stay (first day may be double-weighted for some MS-DRGs); if actual LOS >= geometric mean, allocate full MS-DRG payment to the episode; if less, allocate proportionally and allocate remaining amount to the 90-day post-episode payment calculation. This prevents holding participants responsible for costs that did not overlap with the episode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode assignment for episodes spanning performance years
rubrics_metrics.description: All episodes receive the target price associated with the date of discharge from the anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure, regardless of the episode end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This differs from the original CJR model (which assigned by episode start date) and aligns with BPCI Advanced and TEAM. Annual reconciliation is based on episodes with anchor hospitalization/procedure discharge dates that fall within that performance year. This ensures episodes that begin in one PY and discharge in another are reconciled in the PY of discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capping methodology for target price construction to limit influence of extreme cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply high-cost outlier capping and baseline weighting and capping choices to avoid inflated target prices and protect hospitals from unpredictable catastrophic spending that they could not be expected to prevent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS changed prior methods because the 2-standard-deviation approach allowed more episodes than expected to exceed the cap. The 99th-percentile cap and capping of baseline and performance-year spending are intended to prevent artificial inflation of benchmarks and undue downside risk for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting and rebasing decisions to mitigate the 'ratchet effect'
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose baseline duration, weight recent years more heavily, and roll the baseline forward annually to balance responsiveness to current spending trends against the risk that successful participant improvements will be used to lower future target prices ('ratchet effect').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: shorter, more frequently rebased baselines update target prices faster but risk ratcheting down target prices for successful participants. TEAM's approach (3-year baseline, rebased annually, temporally weighted) is cited as a balance; CJR‑X adopts a similar 3-year temporally weighted baseline to emphasize recent data while moderating the ratchet effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount factor representing Medicare's portion of potential savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a discount factor to benchmark prices when calculating preliminary target prices to represent Medicare's portion of potential savings from the episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discount factor reduces the benchmark to set expectations for shared savings; it is applied alongside the prospective trend and prospective normalization factors in the preliminary target price equation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized payment data and capping at MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type & region level
rubrics_metrics.description: All target price calculations will use standardized payment data and apply caps, trends, normalization, and risk adjustments at the MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes capping at the 99th percentile and calculating risk and trend multipliers at the episode type/region level, producing regionally defined benchmarks and preliminary target prices for each episode type/region combination.
